title: Bidirectional A* on Barcelona: Real-Map Routing ⚡
description: Watch Bidirectional A* on Barcelona’s Eixample grid calculate an optimal route by expanding from both start and goal simultaneously. The result: fewer explored nodes and faster “GPS-style” convergence for real-world pathfinding.
ig_caption:
Bidirectional A* on Real Maps: The Ultimate Pathfinding Algorithm ⚡ How autonomous vehicle routing AI finds the shortest path in milliseconds?

In this visualization, I run Bidirectional A* from both ends:
• Forward search grows from your start node using g(n)+h(n)
• Backward search grows from the goal using the reverse heuristic
• When the frontiers meet, we stitch the best partial paths into one optimal route

Why it’s fast: bidirectional expansion often reduces the explored search space compared to classic A*—especially on large city graphs like Barcelona’s Eixample.

Takeaway: you keep A*’s optimality feel, but you shrink the work by searching “from both sides.”

Debate question: Should autonomous vehicle routing prioritize fewer expanded nodes (speed) or more thorough exploration (robustness) in uncertain traffic?
